content.intro: This lesson focuses on error handling and troubleshooting and connects the PDF syllabus topics to a small, inspectable example. Work from the intended data model, write down the expected result, then verify syntax and semantics with the target tool.
content.why_it_matters: Error Handling and Troubleshooting matters because structured-data files sit between people, tools, services, and deployment systems. A clear contract and repeatable checks make the result easier to maintain and safer to consume.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: Untrusted structured data must be bounded, parsed safely, validated for structure and business meaning, and logged without secrets. YAML custom tags and unsafe constructors require particular care, and errors should fail safely.

content_blocks.title: What you will cover
content_blocks.text: This lesson explicitly addresses: Parser error messages. Schema validation errors. Runtime data errors. Unexpected values. Cross-language inconsistencies.; Reproducing production failures. Building useful diagnostics. Production Practices. Treat each as part of a workflow: define what the data should mean, represent it consistently, and test how the chosen implementation interprets it.

content_blocks.title: Inspectable example: Error Handling and Troubleshooting
content_blocks.code:
Error response checklist:
1. Identify the file and location if available.
2. Distinguish parse errors from schema errors.
3. Report a safe actionable message.
4. Keep stack traces and secret values out of public responses.
content_blocks.expected_output: Useful troubleshooting separates syntax, type/schema, and business-rule failures without leaking sensitive configuration or payload content.

items.title: 1. State the contract
items.text: Write down the expected root type, required fields, scalar types, and any compatibility assumptions.

items.title: 2. Validate before use
items.text: Parse the document and run the applicable schema or policy checks; syntax success alone is not full correctness.

items.title: 3. Test a boundary
items.text: Include at least one missing, malformed, ambiguous, or unexpected input and record the desired behavior.

content_blocks.title: Version and safety checkpoint
content_blocks.text: Treat configuration as code: validate it before use, keep secrets out of the file, review changes, and test both the expected configuration and failure behavior. Confirm implementation-specific behavior against the target parser, tool version, and standards documentation.

content_blocks.title: Try it yourself
content_blocks.text: Create a second synthetic fixture for “Parser error messages. Schema validation errors. Runtime data errors. Unexpected values. Cross-language inconsistencies.”. Predict the parsed types/result, change one relevant detail, and record whether the target tool behaved as expected. Include one invalid or boundary case.

common_mistakes.problem: Treating readable text as proof of correctness.
common_mistakes.why: Syntax and visual formatting cannot establish data types, schema conformance, or application-specific meaning.
common_mistakes.fix: Parse, validate against the intended contract, and test a valid plus an invalid fixture.

common_mistakes.problem: Assuming every parser interprets the feature identically.
common_mistakes.why: Format versions, schema choices, library defaults, and product-specific restrictions affect behavior.
common_mistakes.fix: Record the exact parser/version and test the target environment.

common_mistakes.why: Missing fields, wrong types, duplicate keys, or ambiguous scalars may still break consumers.
common_mistakes.fix: Keep valid, invalid, and boundary fixtures in version control.
